newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Siemens bids for Bucharest heating plant.
newsitem.headline: Siemens bids for Bucharest heating plant.

text.p: Germany's Siemens AG has entered a tender called by Bucharest municipality for the building of an independent power producer in Romania's capital city, a company official said on Tuesday.

"The project involves building of a power station to generate mainly heating to cover a deficit in the northern area of Bucharest, as well as electricity," Dan Pillat from Siemens' Bucharest office told Reuters.
A bid at the tender held on Monday was also made by Amoco together with Electro Invest AB of Sweden, a Bucharest city hall source said on Tuesday.
The successful bidder will be announced by end-October.

If Siemens wins it will become the general contractor for the project financing, together with other investors, consultancy and engineering works on the station, with a right to exploit it for 30 years, Pillat said.
The new plant, to be completed in 2-1/2 years, will use the distribution and transport network of the Renel RA electricity utility and RADET thermal power authority.
The Romanian subsidiary of Electro Invest AB confirmed it had entered a bid together with Amoco.
"After the successful bidder has been announced, studies will be undertaken within a period of three months and then a contract will be signed," Electro Invest's Cornel Cioara said.
Heating supply for Bucharest residents from the city's five thermal stations has been scarce in recent years due to a worn-out, badly-neglected distribution system.
